Site infrastructure funding note: the Coshocton Port Authority received a $58.7M grant (Ohio Dept of Development All Ohio Future Fund, announced July 21, 2025) for utility upgrades, water/wastewater extensions, and roadway improvements across the broader industrial park — this benefits Aligned indirectly but is not a direct subsidy to Aligned and is therefore not listed under subsidies.

energy.notes: Site is in AEP Ohio service territory. Brownfield location retains former plant's high-capacity grid infrastructure, which is a primary site-selection advantage. Aligned is publicly exploring on-site SMR/nuclear additions but no confirmed agreement. Nuclear would be future supplemental supply.

water.notes: No cooling type or water consumption data disclosed. Former coal plant had access to Muskingum River cooling water infrastructure; Aligned has not confirmed whether this will be utilized.

community.notes: Strong positive reception at October 2025 groundbreaking. Coshocton County Commissioners and Port Authority executive director spoke favorably. Site revitalization fills a significant local tax and employment gap left by AEP plant closure (plant formerly provided ~10% of River View Local Schools' annual budget and employed ~600 workers). Broader Ohio policy context: a proposed constitutional amendment that would ban large data centers was under debate at the time of announcement; some community and policy advocates cited this project as evidence of the economic value data centers bring to rural counties.

Site plan application filed May 4, 2026 with fees paid May 18. Up to 8 data centers proposed. No rezoning required (already heavy industry zoning).

Amazon Data Services Inc. formally withdrew its Calvert Technology Center Conceptual Site Development Plan application and decided not to pursue the proposed data center project in Calvert County. Calvert County Government announced the withdrawal in an Aug. 4, 2026 press release; the county's data center page now records the application as withdrawn and states no site plan applications for data center development are pending. The withdrawal followed voter backlash in the county's June 23, 2026 primary, and the county subsequently passed a six-month moratorium on data center site plan approvals effective Aug. 28, 2026.

notes: Codename 'Project Green'; application filed via NorthPoint Development, LLC. Two-phase build-out: Phase 1 = 8 data center buildings; Phase 2 = 13 additional buildings (21 total). Located on ~1,000 acres at northeast quadrant of I-70 and Highway 19 interchange near New Florence. Official AWS/Governor Kehoe announcement on June 15, 2026 cited a $10B investment commitment. Earlier county planning documents and initial filings referenced a maximum capital investment ceiling of up to $35B — that figure is a speculative ceiling, not a committed amount. AWS separately announced a 138MW renewable energy project in Missouri; not confirmed as dedicated to this campus. Community investments included in announcement: $3M for county 911/emergency dispatch upgrades, $3M for community programs, $1M for Montgomery County Fairgrounds, $150K community fund, $50K teacher grant. Preserve Montgomery County LLC filed suit in February 2026 alleging ten counts of Missouri Sunshine Law violations (closed-session negotiations, NDAs with Amazon); case pending as of mid-2026. First buildings targeted operational by 2027; full campus potentially complete ~2032. Coordinates are approximate (parcel centroid at I-70 / Hwy 19 NE quadrant). Jobs: KOMU reported ~400 permanent jobs; DCD's coverage of the same $10B announcement cited no specific permanent figure (only 'thousands of construction jobs') — permanent count left unstructured pending firm corroboration.

energy.notes: Powered by Ameren Missouri grid. AWS committed to working with Ameren to ensure project energy costs are not passed to other ratepayers. AWS announced a separate 138MW renewable energy project in Missouri (not confirmed as on-site or dedicated to this campus).

water.notes: Water sourced from Cambrian-Ordovician aquifer via wells drilled to ~1,500 ft depth (to avoid impacting local private wells at shallower depths). Initial phase projected at 2.9M gallons/year; full 17-building campus projected at ~50M gallons/year (~0.137 MGD equivalent). Regional aquifer capacity exceeds 23 trillion gallons; current regional utilization ~8%; this project adds ~0.03%. On-site stormwater management ponds and water treatment plant planned. Cooling methodology not publicly specified.

subsidies.program: Montgomery County Chapter 100 bond / PILOT — personal property tax abatements on declining schedule approved December 2025; real property taxes paid in full; public safety districts (ambulance, fire) opted out and retain full allocations. Total multi-year abatement value not publicly disclosed.

community.notes: Preserve Montgomery County LLC (coalition of local residents, farmers, and business owners) filed a 10-count lawsuit in February 2026 alleging Missouri Sunshine Law violations — specifically that county commissioners conducted negotiations in closed sessions and signed NDAs with Amazon. Community concerns at public meetings included water usage impacts, potential electric rate increases, and loss of rural character. Some residents and officials expressed support for the project's economic benefits. Construction proceeded despite the pending suit. Montgomery County Commission stated real property taxes are not abated and projected the project would double the county's tax revenue at full buildout.

Design-builder Cascade Nuclear Partners (Kiewit Nuclear Solutions / Black & Veatch / Aecon) selected 2025. Amazon separately anchored a ~$500M Series C-1 investment in X-energy (announced 2024-10-16, alongside Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, Citadel's Ken Griffin, Ares Management affiliates, NGP, and the University of Michigan) supporting X-energy's reactor design/licensing and Phase 1 of its TRISO-X fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge, TN -- this is company-level X-energy funding, not Cascade project capex. Standard Permit Modification Application, Registration No. 177263 (Abilene DC 1, LLC dba Crusoe Energy Systems)

notes: On-site behind-the-meter natural-gas generation for the co-located Crusoe / Lancium Clean Campus ('Stargate Site 1', tracked separately as lancium-crusoe-abilene-tx). 10 turbines totaling 360.5 MW are permit-confirmed (TCEQ Reg. 177263) and reported operational as of mid-2026, with a large expansion proposed. energy.notes: Behind-the-meter, primary-plus-backup on-site generation dedicated to the campus; explicitly not exporting to ERCOT.

emissions.unitsCovered: ten (10) natural gas-fired simple cycle combustion turbines: five Solar Titan 350 (TURBINE-1 through TURBINE-5) and five GE LM2500 (TURBINE-6 through TURBINE-10)
emissions.notes: NO per-pollutant annual tonnage is recorded here, deliberately. This is a TCEQ Electric Generating Unit Standard Permit registration — a rule-based authorisation that does not state per-pollutant tons-per-year ceilings the way a PSD or plan-approval permit does. The only annual tonnages in the file are the applicant's own calculated potential-to-emit (Table 1(a) of the modification application, built from manufacturer rates and AP-42 emission factors), and potential-to-emit is not a permitted ceiling; this project does not publish one as the other. The enforceable limit the standard permit does impose is a RATE: 0.14 lb NOx/MWh for units operating more than 300 hours per year, against which the application estimates a controlled rate of 0.09 lb/MWh. Registration history: originally registered 2024-08-30 for six Titan 350 plus six GE LM2500; the modification approved 2025-01-22 reduced each model from six to five, giving the ten turbines above (Titan 350 site-rated 38 MW each, GE LM2500 34.1 MW each). Registered as Abilene DC 1, LLC dba Crusoe Energy Systems (Regulated Entity RN112029079, Customer CN606295137). A separate major TCEQ permit application filed July 2026 seeking roughly 41 additional turbines is NOT covered by this registration and none of its figures are recorded here.

generation.notes: TCEQ Standard Permit Technical Review (Registration 177263, approved 2025-01-22) confirms 10 simple-cycle turbines — 5x Solar Titan 350 (~38 MW) + 5x GE LM2500 (~34.1 MW) = 360.5 MW — behind-the-meter for on-site compute, no grid export. A proposed expansion (major TCEQ permit filed Jul 2026, not yet approved) would add 41 turbines (~1.4 GW) plus 18 diesel gensets; the ~1.2 GW figure often cited for the campus describes IT/interconnect capacity, not generation nameplate. Gas-plant buildout cost reported at ~$500M, distinct from the ~$1.1B data-center project figure.

Investment: equipment financing commitments exceed $600M ($500M MUFG turbine warehouse + $200M Keystone/Cape facility); projected total project cost $70–90B is a range/projection, not a firm figure — omitted from investmentUsd per data-rigor policy. Jobs: 50,000+ projected across campus lifetime — projection only, omitted from jobs field. Nuclear campus name in NRC COLA filings: 'President Donald J. Trump Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus'; publicly marketed as Project Matador / HyperGrid.

energy.notes: Initial generation: on-site natural gas. Fermi acquired 600MW+ of gas turbines in two deals (July 2025): 478MW from Firebird LNG/Siemens Energy (six SGT800 turbines + heat recovery steam generators + one SST600 steam turbine) and 135MW from GE 6B Frame units acquired from a New Jersey facility. TCEQ issued preliminary approval for up to 6GW of combined-cycle gas (November 2025); air permit secured February 2026 after ~279 public comments. Long-term plan adds four Westinghouse AP1000 reactors (~4.4GW nuclear baseload; COLA filed June 17 2025, NRC accepted two of three parts for review September 2025, Part 3 deadline December 31 2026, first reactor targeted 2031, all four by 2038) plus solar and battery storage. Fermi is also evaluating SMRs (MOU with Doosan Enerbility). Entire campus is behind-the-meter — private grid, no public utility offtake.

water.notes: No confirmed water use figures published. Community opposition raised concerns about Ogallala Aquifer impacts from combined cooling demand of gas plants and data centers. Arid Texas Panhandle location heightens water supply risk.

community.notes: TCEQ air permit process (for 93 planned gas turbines) drew 279+ public comments, majority opposed. 63 contested case hearing requests filed before State Office of Administrative Hearings; 21 additional public meeting requests. Primary opposition group: Panhandle Taxpayers for Transparency. Key concerns: air quality (modeled 2,140 tpy CO and 1,591 tpy NOx), water demand, impacts on farmland and nearby cattle operations (Tyson Foods facility adjacent). Fermi bused in college students to a December 2025 public meeting, stoking further controversy.

notes: Represented here as a single aggregate record rather than N per-site entries: MARA discloses this program only in aggregate (25 MW total across Texas + North Dakota wellheads), with no per-site count, capacity breakdown, or coordinates published — consistent with a genuinely mobile/modular operating model (containerized generators moved between wellheads as flaring economics shift at individual wells), not merely underreported. energy.notes: Captures gas that would otherwise be flared/vented at oil & gas wellheads and combusts it in generators to power mining hardware — framed by MARA as reducing methane venting (methane → CO2 combustion swap), not as a zero-emissions source.

notes: Officially "PORTS-Pike Technology Campus"; formerly tracked under the pre-announcement Ohio entity New Day Data Centers LLC, a name that appears nowhere in the SEC S-1 or SB Energy’s own announcements. Developer/operator is SB Energy (SoftBank-controlled); the DOE lease was signed 2026-02-26 by its subsidiary Pike County Portsmouth DC LLC. CAPACITY - three distinct figures that must not be conflated: 8.0 GW-IT of contracted compute (8,024 MW-IT; NVIDIA guarantees the initial 4.25 GW-IT with an option on the remaining 3.78 GW-IT), 10 GW of gross power load (the capacityMw.planned value here), and 9.2 GW of new gas generation. OFFTAKE: on 2026-08-17 SB Energy subsidiaries signed 17 twenty-year triple-net leases with OpenAI, with rent commencement conditioned on interconnection and generation being available; NVIDIA provided a residual-value guaranty capped at $105B and separately bought $1.5B of non-voting stock. LAND: landAcres is intentionally omitted - the DOE lease covers 189 acres (Batch 1) on which "one data center building is expected to be constructed", while the S-1 places the buildings "across several thousand acres of private property"; the widely-cited 3,700/3,777 acres is the whole federal reservation, which also hosts the separately tracked Oklo Aurora project, Centrus and the DUF6 plant. INVESTMENT: investmentUsd intentionally omitted - $10B (DOE, March) and $30-40B (project site) describe the same ~800 MW first phase and cannot both be right, the $67.2B total appears only as one trade outlet’s unattributed rollup, and the S-1 states no total capex. SUBSIDIES: none awarded - the Ohio Tax Credit Authority minutes record no award, no JobsOhio award was found, and Ohio paused new data-centre tax exemptions in May 2026; a county PILOT is under negotiation because the leased federal land yields no property tax. STATUS: early civil works began after the 2026-03-20 groundbreaking, though the S-1 lists construction as not started, with first capacity in 2028 and full buildout 2032. Distinct from oklo-aurora-pike-county-oh on the same broader site - do not merge or double-count.

energy.notes: S-1: the campus is "designed to include 8.0 GW-IT of data center capacity, representing 10 GW of gross power load expected to be supported by the PJM transmission system and new neighbouring gas-fired generation facilities" - hence "mixed". The 9.2 GW of gas is new build, not a reused plant; the site is the former Portsmouth uranium-enrichment complex, whose historic power came over OVEC coal-fired transmission (X-533 switchyard, de-energised 2008, decommissioned 2011). Recorded under onSiteGenerationMw as dedicated captive generation, but note the S-1 calls the plants "neighbouring": they sit ~5 miles south of Piketon adjacent to the DOE site, are developed by "an affiliate of SoftBank that is not our subsidiary", and SB Energy "do[es] not expect to own or operate" them. Ohio Power Siting Board case 26-0746-EL-BGN (applicant Portsmouth Gas DevCo, LLC) covers only a first tranche of "up to 2 gigawatts"; AEP Ohio transmission (new 765 kV Baku-Gavin line and four substations) is a separate docket. AEP grid capex is stated as $4.2B by DOE and ~$5.1B in the S-1, unreconciled. CAUTION: the project site states the gas generation "will be owned by the U.S. Government", but the S-1 says "no binding agreement has been executed between us or any of our affiliates and any governmental entity with respect to the funding, construction, ownership or operation of the generation facilities" - do not assert federal ownership. Only ~0.8 GW of gross load has contracted utility service so far.

community.notes: Documented local support alongside contamination-legacy distrust. Support: State Sen. Shane Wilkin - "It’s just going to be a generational change for this area"; SODI executive director Steve Shepherd called it "a model for the country"; the Scioto Valley-Piketon Area Council of Governments chair framed it as moving contaminated residential land to industrial use. Concern: a neighbouring farmer with contaminated property ("This is the most contaminated place around here"), and Conserve Ohio on water, transmission and the precedent of siting hyperscale projects on legacy DOE land. No litigation, moratorium or public-hearing defeat found as of 2026-09-01; a statewide watchdog notes this project lacks the named opposition groups seen elsewhere in Ohio. Community money (not a public subsidy to the operator): a $40M Community Benefits Agreement from SB Energy plus an incremental $40M from OpenAI.

It reimburses the developer for six enumerated regional infrastructure components it builds and dedicates to the city — two public-safety sites, temporary and permanent public-safety facilities, $15M toward the Johnson Road interchange, and oversized regional water infrastructure — funded by 20% of the tax revenue the project itself generates, beginning only after the city has received $60M cumulatively and terminating 20 years from the effective date. It is capped at "the lesser of" the developer's verified costs or $50,000,000, so it cannot exceed what the developer actually spent; it is cost recovery for public infrastructure rather than an incentive, abatement or credit, and is therefore not recorded as a subsidy. Nothing has been paid to date. Buckeye's economic-development director has projected "more than 360 jobs at full build out" — an end-state across as many as 40 separate future data centers, none yet leased, permitted or built, and so not recorded as a permanent-jobs figure for this site. notes: Former Duke Energy site on Stanton Rd, Southaven. ~46 turbines operational by May 2026; permitting contested — 41 permitted Mar 2026, additional turbines unpermitted; NAACP/Earthjustice/SELC litigation. Distinct facility from the separately tracked xAI Southaven data center (Colossus).

emissions.unitsCovered: forty-one (41) natural gas-fired simple cycle combustion turbines: seventeen Solar Titan Model PGM-130 (TUR-1 through TUR-17), sixteen Solar Titan Model 350 (TUR-18 through TUR-33), and eight ProEnergy Model 6000PE (TUR-34 through TUR-41)
emissions.notes: Permitted CEILINGS from MDEQ PSD Air Construction Permit 0680-00119 (permittee MZX Tech LLC, an xAI affiliate; AI 12592), not measured emissions. Every per-group tonnage is PER TURBINE on a 12-month rolling total basis — they are limits on each individual machine and must never be summed or multiplied by the unit count to state a facility total; the permit itself states no facility-wide tonnage for NOx, CO, VOC, SO2, PM10, PM2.5, NH3 or formaldehyde. SCOPE CAVEAT: this permit authorises 41 turbines, while this record's generation.unitCount of 59 describes the larger on-site fleet, which includes turbines operating without this permit and is the subject of NAACP/SELC/Earthjustice litigation filed 2026-04-14. The two counts measure different things and must not be reconciled by editing either. GHG: the permit sets CO2 as a rate only — BACT of 120 lb/MMBtu, short-term and long-term — with NO annual tonnage cap, so co2e is deliberately left undefined; a missing co2e here does not mean the facility has no GHG limit. HAPs: the only facility-wide caps in the permit are 24.0 tpy total combined HAPs and 9.50 tpy for any individual HAP (Condition 3.3, "For the entire facility"); the schema records the combined figure, and the per-individual cap has no field. The permit prints formaldehyde as "CH2O"; PM10 and PM2.5 are stated as filterable + condensable.

energy.notes: About 35 on-site natural-gas turbines (a combined 422 MW per SELC and aerial imagery) supplement a 150 MW grid substation and Tesla Megapack storage. The Shelby County Health Department permitted only 15 turbines; an SELC/NAACP appeal stays that permit. xAI said the Phase-I temporary turbines would be demobilized after grid connection, but 2025 aerial imagery shows 35 on site.

water.notes: The open cooling loop's design draw is roughly 3 MGD from the Memphis Sands aquifer via MLGW (xAI engineer, per Governing), though Protect Our Aquifer reported a lower early-operational actual of ~0.8 MGD (~812,000 gal/day) in early 2025 as the site was still ramping. xAI broke ground in Oct 2025 on an $80M greywater-recycling plant at the T.E. Maxson wastewater facility (targeting ~10 MGD of treated wastewater); construction was later paused.

community.notes: The NAACP (with SELC and Earthjustice) sued xAI over roughly 35 unpermitted methane gas turbines; the county permitted only 15, and the NAACP/SELC appeal to the Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board stays it. The permit drew 1,700+ public comments, most opposed, and South Memphis (Boxtown) residents already face elevated asthma and cancer rates. xAI did not pursue a Shelby County EDGE PILOT tax abatement; no public subsidy is on record.

stakeholders.note: Runs xAI, the company operating this facility; CNBC, reporting the Shelby County turbine-permit appeal, describes "xAI, which is run by Elon Musk" as having set up in Memphis in 2024.
